charts.grid: horizontal only, var(--grid), no axis lines or tick marks, ticks 12px var(--text-muted)

sourceFlowBranches.quarantine: 1.5px var(--status-critical), dasharray 3 4, opacity 0.7, into a var(--tint-critical) node
sourceFlowBranches.duplicates: 1.5px var(--text-muted), dasharray 1 4, round caps, opacity 0.8, into a var(--surface-2) node

charts.cityMap: viewBox 0 0 440 410, schematic positions; .city-name 18 / 500 and .city-value 16, in viewBox units

extensions.icons: One inline SVG set (components/Icon.tsx): 24px grid, 1.75 stroke, round caps and joins, paths after Lucide (ISC); decorative unless labelled.
extensions.status: lib/status.ts: one TONES table maps every backend and source-health status to tone, icon and label; toneOf() serves non-badge uses (layer map).

narrative.overview:
RideOps reads like a printed operations report that keeps its receipts. Each page is a column of bands under hairline rules (Sources, then Checks, then Results on the Overview), and every band names the table it was computed from in small mono type beside its heading. The figures are large, tabular and quiet; the lineage is small and always present. Density is that of a working tool: 14-15px text, 16px gutters, tables with 9px cell padding, nothing padded for show.

The world is shared with the landing page at `/` (`frontend/index.html`): a white ground, one warm near-black ink used for text, primary actions and the sidebar band, a single mint accent, Familjen Grotesk for everything with IBM Plex Mono for identifiers, small sharp corners and hairlines in place of shadows. The landing page draws on its own kit in `frontend/public/assets`; this document covers the dashboard at `/app` (`frontend/src`) only, and the two meet in fonts, ink, mint and corner language rather than in shared components.

Colour does jobs, never decoration. The five source applications each own one hue, the six cities each own one series slot, the four state tones tint fills and badges, and mint marks only where you are and what is healthy. Everything else is ink on white, or white on near-black in dark mode.
keyCharacteristics: Ink band sidebar (#232323 light, #141414 dark) with the active page filled mint.
Reports built from bands with a hairline section head and a mono lineage line.
Flat surfaces: 1px hairline borders, no shadows at rest; tints carry state.
Familjen Grotesk at two weights (400, 500), tabular figures for every number; IBM Plex Mono only for table, file and pipeline names.
Corners at 6-8px for containers and controls, 2-4px for data marks, full pills only for badges and meters.
Entity colour is fixed: a source or a city keeps its hue on every page and in both themes.
Light by default (like the landing page), with Dark and System one select away in the sidebar footer.

rules.name: The Jobs-Only Colour Rule
rules.body: A hue appears only when it identifies a source, a city or a state. Nothing is coloured to make a section look lively.

rules.name: The Mint Means Here-and-Healthy Rule
rules.body: Mint fills the active place (current nav item) and confirms health (API connected, validated tables). It is not a highlight colour for figures, cards or headings.

rules.name: The Fixed Entity Rule
rules.body: Colour follows the entity, never its rank: a city or source keeps the same slot when filters remove its neighbours, in every chart and both themes.

rules.name: The Never-Alone Rule
rules.body: State colour always travels with an icon and a label (StatusBadge, or an icon-led count such as "check 12 pass"), and every chart with two or more series carries a legend and a table view. Three light-theme categorical slots sit under 3:1 against the surface, which is why the legend and table are mandatory, not optional.

rules.name: The Two Weights Rule
rules.body: Familjen Grotesk runs at 400 and 500 only. Emphasis comes from size and colour, not bold.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number that can be compared (KPI values, facts, table numeric columns, tooltip values, bar list values) uses `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, and numeric table columns align right.

rules.name: The Mono Is an Identifier Rule
rules.body: IBM Plex Mono marks names that exist in the system: `ops.ingestion_log`, `monitoring/incidents/*.md`, a pipeline name. It is never used for labels, numbers or decoration.

rules.name: The Report Column Rule
rules.body: A page is one column of named sections read top to bottom; side-by-side placement happens only inside a section, never between sections.

rules.name: The Hairline-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Containers separate with a 1px `border` hairline or a change of surface, never with a shadow. Only transient overlays (the chart tooltip) cast one.

rules.name: The Pill Is a Tag Rule
rules.body: Only badges and meters are pills. Anything a user clicks or reads as a container keeps its 6-8px corner.

dos: Do open each section with its hairline head and name its source tables in the lineage line, in mono (`ops.data_quality_results`).
Do give every chart a Chart / Table segmented switch and a legend once it has two series.
Do take city colours from the fixed series order and source colours from `--src-*`, so an entity never changes hue between pages.
Do tint the whole KPI tile (good, warning, critical) when the number is itself a state, and drop its border when you do.
Do pair every state colour with an icon and a label through StatusBadge, and mark simulated figures with the dashed Simulated badge.
Do keep containers at 8px, controls at 6px, data marks at 2-4px.
Do set every comparable number in tabular figures and right-align numeric columns.
Do keep text on mint in Workshop Ink (#232323), in both themes.
donts: Don't add drop shadows to cards, tiles, columns or the sidebar; only the transient chart tooltip floats.
Don't use mint to highlight a figure, card or heading; it marks the active place and healthy confirmations only.
Don't colour an element that does not identify a source, a city or a state.
Don't use IBM Plex Mono for labels, numbers or decoration.
Don't set Familjen Grotesk above 500 weight.
Don't make a button, card or chip a pill; pills are for badges and meters.
Don't let state colour stand alone as the only signal.
